summary: The reader has finished an undergraduate computer science degree: asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, gcd, floor and ceiling, binary representation, finite sets and subsets, basic induction and recurrences), linear algebra (vectors, matrices, inverses, orthogonality, rank, over the reals), basic number theory and algebra (rings of integers mod m, primes), and the basics of algorithm analysis including divide and conquer and schoolbook multiplication. They know Turing machines and tapes at a basic level. They have not studied fast integer multiplication, finite fields, abstract ring theory, Lie-type matrix factorizations, or the research literature on Fourier-based multiplication.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers taken modulo m, with a congruent to b mod m when m divides a-b.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: Two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1, which is the condition for being invertible modulo each other.

known.name: Floor and ceiling functions and integer division
known.gloss: The floor of x is the largest integer not exceeding x, and integer division gives quotient and remainder a = bq + r.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits, and the value of the string is the sum of bit times power of two.

known.name: Logarithms and iterated logarithms
known.gloss: lg n is the base-2 logarithm and log log n iterates it; they are standard growth-rate functions.

known.name: Schoolbook integer multiplication
known.gloss: Multiplying two n-digit numbers digit by digit with shifted partial sums in O(n^2) time.

known.name: Karatsuba and divide-and-conquer multiplication
known.gloss: Splitting integers into halves and using fewer than four half-size products gives a subquadratic multiplication.

known.name: Recurrence relations and master theorem
known.gloss: Running times of recursive algorithms satisfy recurrences solved by unrolling or by the master theorem.

known.name: Linear algebra over the reals
known.gloss: Vectors, matrices, matrix products, inverses, rank and orthogonality, including linear maps given by matrices.

known.name: Triangular matrices and Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Matrices with zeros above or below the diagonal, and row reduction of a matrix by elementary operations.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A bijection of a finite set to itself, composed and inverted as functions.

known.name: Cartesian product of sets
known.gloss: The set of tuples with each coordinate drawn from its own set, used to index multidimensional arrays.

known.name: Finite sets, subsets and indicator vectors
known.gloss: A subset of a ground set is encoded by a 0/1 vector, with intersection sizes given by dot products.

known.name: Exclusive or and bitwise operations
known.gloss: XOR is addition of bits modulo 2, applied coordinatewise to bit strings.

known.name: Prime numbers and factorization
known.gloss: Integers greater than 1 with no proper divisors, and the unique factorization of integers into primes.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, residues modulo each determine a unique residue modulo their product.

known.name: Primitive roots of unity
known.gloss: Complex numbers whose nth power is 1, such as e^{2 pi i/n}, whose powers are evenly spaced on the unit circle.

known.name: Rings and quotient by a polynomial
known.gloss: A set with addition and multiplication satisfying the usual laws, such as the integers mod m or polynomials reduced mod a fixed polynomial.

known.name: Absolute value and norm of complex numbers
known.gloss: The size of a complex number or vector, used to bound errors.

known.name: Rounding and error bounds
known.gloss: Rounding a real approximation to the nearest integer recovers the exact value when the error is below 1/2.

known.name: Dyadic rationals
known.gloss: Rationals of the form m/2^k, representable exactly with finitely many bits.

known.name: Fixed-point and fixed-width numbers
known.gloss: Numbers stored as integers times a fixed power of two, giving a fixed number of bits of precision.

known.name: Finite automata and finite-state control
known.gloss: A machine with a fixed finite set of states and a fixed finite alphabet.

known.name: Sorting and linear-time scans
known.gloss: Sorting in n log n time and linear passes over data as basic algorithmic building blocks.

known.name: Gates and circuits
known.gloss: A fixed network of operations on wires computing a function from inputs to outputs, as in digital logic.

known.name: Induction and recursion
known.gloss: Proof and algorithm structure in which a problem is reduced to smaller instances of itself.

known.name: Constants and parameter choice in asymptotic bounds
known.gloss: Standard asymptotic notations O, Omega, Theta and o and the use of fixed constant exponents.
